summary: - _(c) Declare / hold that the Petitioner Company is entitled for interest of Rs. 86,35,87,699/- for delay in payment of Capacity Charges and Energy Charges for the Bill Nos. 3A, 4A, SA, 6A, 7A, and 8 in terms of Power Purchase Agreement dated 31.3.1997 from 9.2.2001 till the date of filing of this Petition and consequently direct the respondents 1 to 6 to pay the same;_ 4. Pursuant to the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 (w.e.f. from 1.3.2014), apart from the AP Discoms (Respondents 4 & 6), the Telangana Discoms (Respondents 3 & 5) succeeded the rights and obligations under the PPA to the part contracted capacity, viz., 335 MW. These Respondents are collectively referred to as ‘Respondent Discoms’, in this order. Subsequently, this Petition (O.P. No. 33/2009) was renumbered as O.P. No. 27/2015. The Respondents have filed their counter affidavit on 3.12.2013, and the Petitioner has filed its rejoinder on 20.12.2013. During the pendency of this Petition, the Hon’ble Supreme Court in C.A. Nos. 3788-3790/2019 (APEPDCL & anr v GMRVPGL & ors) vide order dated 4.2.2020, upheld the jurisdiction of the Central Commission to decide the cases involving the disputes between the Respondent Discoms and the Generating Company. In this regard, the Telangana State Electricity Regulatory Commission (TSERC), vide its order dated 29.5.2021, transferred the various Petitions to this Commission, in addition to Petition O.P. No. 27/2015. Thereafter, this Commission vide letter dated 10.8.2021, called upon the 6. The Petition was admitted on 14.2.2023, and the Commission, after issuing notice to the Respondents, directed the parties to complete their pleadings in the matter. In compliance with the directions, the Respondent Discoms filed their replies vide separate affidavits dated 20.3.2023. 11. During the hearing of this petition, along with the batch cases, the Commission, while granting time to the Respondents to file their written submissions, sought certain other additional information. In compliance with the said directions, LKPL and the Respondents have filed the additional information on 1.12.2023 and 18.12.2023, respectively. The Respondent Discoms vide affidavit dated 27.1.2024 filed its written submissions, mainly reiterating their submissions in its reply / additional information. However, the Respondents have referred to the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in APTRANSCO v GMRVPGL & ors (2018) 3 SCC 716, and submitted that, when the parties by their conduct have put a particular interpretation of the agreement, the same is binding and there is no requirement of any further inquiry as to the actual interpretation. 13. During the hearing, the parties requested that the present petition, along with the batch matters, be specially listed for hearing. The Commission, after directing the parties to file their note of submissions (not exceeding four pages), including the 16. During the hearing, the learned Senior counsel for LKPL, pointed out to its written submissions and submitted that the issues raised in the batch petitions, relate to tariff and are, therefore, not referable to arbitration, in the light of the APTEL judgement dated 25.10.2024 in MPPMCL v DVC (Appeal No.309/2024) as affirmed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court. At the request of the parties, this petition (Petition No.249/MP/2022) was heard, and the Commission, after directing the Respondents to file certain additional information/submissions and for LKPL to file its response, reserved its order. The Respondents have filed their additional submissions vide affidavit dated 3.7.2025, and LKPL has filed its response dated 12.7.2025. _**Issue No. (B):** Whether the dispute in the present case is to be adjudicated by this Commission or referred to arbitration?_ _“Having considered submissions of the parties we find no merit in the aforesaid contention advanced on behalf of appellant. The view which we are going to take has been indicated by this Court in several judgments including_ _**M.P. Steel Corporation** (supra). But the point requires no debate in view of clear stipulation in explanation (a) to sub-section (3) of Section 14 of the Limitation Act._ ## _**Issue No. (B): Whether the dispute in the present case is to be adjudicated by this Commission or to be referred to arbitration?**_ ## 24. The Respondents have submitted that the main dispute between the parties is its order dated 23.9.2024 in C.A.No.10480/2024. Admittedly, the dispute in the present _24. Thus, in a case before the CERC involving generating companies or transmission licensee, where the dispute is connected with matters listed under Section 79(1)(a)-(d), the CERC may choose to itself adjudicate upon the dispute or refer the same for arbitration._ _(i) After considering the various rulings of the Hon'ble Supreme Court referred to above and the circumstances of the case we have come to the conclusion that the State Commission having come to the conclusion that the Petition filed by the respondents 2 to 7 was barred by limitation, had no jurisdiction to decide the matter on merits holding_ 42. We have examined the rival submissions. Though objections have been raised by LKPL with regard to the duration of the PPA raised by the Respondents in the present proceedings, on the ground being a subsequent event, we examine the same, as it has a material bearing on the entitlement/obligation of the Respondents. The contention of the Respondents that the parties have acted on the basis of the Project COD as 2.1.2001 [as in para 40 (i) above], deserves no merit for consideration. As
title: Petition for seeking direction to the Respondents to pay capacity charges and interest on delay in payment of capacity charges and energy charges in terms of PPA dated 31.3.1997. M/s Lanco Kondapalli Power Limited
